title: WarrantArtifact
description: PROPOSED, NOT ADMITTED. A recomputable record of what a logic kernel established over a supplied ground set. It records logic only: it does not assert source authenticity, institutional authority, admission, or an execution decision. A warrant is an input to a runtime decision, never the decision itself. See adr/ADR-013.md and docs/contracts/WARRANT-CONTRACT-v0.1.md.

kernel_digest.description: A digest emitted by the logic kernel. ZTL v0.1 canonicalises with an RFC 8785 (JCS) float-free subset and digests with SHA-384, so sha384 is permitted here even though OIC's own artifact hashing is SHA-256 only in v0.1. OIC records this value; it does not recompute it.

warrant_artifact_id.description: Stable identifier for this warrant artifact.

schema_version.description: Version of this proposed schema the artifact was produced against.

claim_id.description: Identifier of the admitted proposition the warrant is about. Binds the warrant to a claim, not to a document.

formula.description: The propositional formula the kernel evaluated, as the kernel rendered it. Recorded verbatim for replay; OIC does not parse it.

formula_hash.description: Kernel digest over the canonicalised formula and its atoms. A runtime decision must confirm this matches the formula bound to the control; a mismatch means the warrant is about a different proposition.

disposition.description: The kernel's primary operational signal. OPEN means the grounds do not settle the claim. OPEN MUST NEVER be read as falsity: see ADR-013 and the raw-verdict warning below.

raw_verdict.description: The kernel's internal truth marking. RECORDED FOR REPLAY ONLY. It MUST NOT drive any OIC decision. ZTL can return raw_verdict 'F' together with disposition 'OPEN' (measured: judge("p & q", {p:T, q:Z})). An adapter reading this field alone converts 'not yet established' into 'established false', violating invariant I-03.

warranty_grade.description: How durable the result is under further verification. 'hereditary' is invariant under every admissible monotone refinement of the same formula and marking; 'sound' never lies but may stall; 'until-verification' holds only in the present marking. hereditary implies sound. This is half of the result, not optional metadata.

unverified_ground_ids.description: Atom or proposition identifiers the kernel could not verify. Always surfaced as missing_ground_ids on the runtime decision, including when the outcome is ALLOW.

dependency_ids.description: Ground identifiers the conclusion depends on. Used for revocation and expiry propagation.

ground_epoch.description: Monotone counter of the ground set this warrant was computed against. A tick is the arrival of ground; an anti-tick is ground withdrawn. A decision evaluated at a different epoch cannot reuse this warrant without recomputation.

ground_set_hash.description: Digest of the exact ground set supplied to the kernel. Detects staleness that an epoch counter alone would miss.

source_anchor_ids.description: Source anchors for the grounds. Supplied to the kernel by OIC; the kernel does not read documents.

admission_ids.description: Admission records that made these grounds usable. Logic over unadmitted grounds is not a warrant for anything (I-02).

kernel_commit.description: Immutable commit of the kernel that produced this artifact.

input_hash.description: Digest of the exact kernel input, for replay.

output_hash.description: Digest of the exact kernel output, for replay.

valid_until.description: Explicit scoped expiry. Null means no time-based expiry was declared, which is NOT the same as 'never expires': revocation and epoch change still invalidate. Unrestricted expiry trivialises warranties, so expiry is scoped rather than global.

revocation_references.description: Revocation records that would invalidate this warrant if present and in force.

recomputation_reference.description: How to recompute this warrant deterministically: pinned kernel, input hash, and ground set. Required so a warrant is evidence rather than an assertion.

limitations.description: What this warrant does NOT establish. Required and non-empty on purpose: a warrant with no stated ceiling invites over-reading.
